title: What's new
subtitle: Every Kolo release — from the first version to today.

footer.title: Have an idea for Kolo?

versions.title: Kolo in your language
versions.intro: Kolo is learning new languages too: the app is being translated into German, Spanish, French and Portuguese, and on your first visit the site greets you in the language of your country. And if you're starting Norwegian or English, there are now ready-made word sets: a whole topic in one tap.

features.title: Your language from the first visit
features.text: The first time you open Kolo, the site appears in the language of the country you're in, worked out from your device's time zone: nothing is sent anywhere and no location access is needed. If your browser is set to one of our languages, that one wins. Once you log in, the language stays put, even when you travel, and you can change it any time in Settings or at the bottom of the welcome page.

features.title: Ready-made word sets
features.text: If you're learning Norwegian or English, Words now has two tabs: “My sets” and “Kolo sets”. The second holds 16 themed sets for level A1, from greetings and numbers to food, work and the weather: 346 Norwegian words and 355 English ones, each with an example and translations into seven languages. Open a topic to look through its words and add it, or take the whole level with “Add all”. The sets go into their own folder and are yours to edit like any other, and new words come in at your own pace, so nothing piles up. In “First steps” on Home, Kolo now suggests a ready-made set first, and creating your own is still one tap away. Medals for words and sets now count only the words you've started, so a level added in one tap doesn't earn them on its own.

features.title: Spotted a mistake?
features.text: Kolo sets are brand new and haven't been proofread line by line yet, so a word, a translation or an example may be off. Tap “Report a mistake” under the word list in a set's preview, or the flag on a card in a set you took from Kolo, and tell us what's wrong: the message goes straight to the team, and we'll fix it in the next version of the set.

features.title: A tidier Words screen
features.text: Folders are now a single row of compact chips above your sets, each with its colour, name and number of sets. On a phone the row scrolls sideways, so a few folders no longer push your sets down the screen, and you can still drop a set onto a folder. The phone header fits on one line too, with round buttons for a new folder and a new set on the right.

features.title: Share your orbit
features.text: Your weekly orbit can now become a picture for social media or a chat: the ring with your streak, the days of this week, your record and level, in a light, warm or night style. Look for Share in your profile, in the week card at the top of the screen and right when an orbit closes.

fixes: The Log in button is now in the site header on phones too.

Medal progress now counts the same way as the medals themselves, by the words and sets you've started, so a bar no longer sits full next to a locked medal. Home and your profile show the same number of medals.

Profile stats now include Blitz rounds, and the counter that said “Flashcard sessions” is named for what it counts: Perigee and flashcard sessions. A Blitz round now earns the first-session medal too.
A set's page shows its plan, with strong, growing, learning and new words, instead of “Learned”, which counted any word after a single right answer.

versions.title: Orbits, capsules and a course for every language
versions.intro: The biggest Kolo update yet. Daily flames have made way for weekly orbits, practising now earns you rewards, and every language gets its own course.

features.title: Perigee sessions
features.text: One button on the home screen starts a short session across all the sets in your course: up to 20 words, 3–5 minutes. Perigee first shows you new words, then asks you to spot them among options, and checks familiar ones by how well you know them — with options, typing, a flashcard, a gap in the example sentence or by ear. A mistake comes back a few steps later until it sticks. Each of the four ratings has its own timing: “Don't know” shows the word again later in the same session, “Forgot” — tomorrow, “Remember” — in a few days, “Know” — the latest. The timing is shown under each button, and a rated card flies off to the side. Answers in the Quiz and Blitz now count towards your schedule too — those modes carry the Perigee mark. Inside a set, the Learn button starts the same session with just that set's words. There are fewer modes now, each with its own job: Survival, Match pairs and the separate daily review are gone — the Perigee session replaces them. Every step now sits on a question card, like in the quiz, with the word's strength and the set it comes from, and the header shows what's in the session: how many words to review and how many are new. Not sure? “I don't know” is there too. Right answers in a row build a streak, and the summary tells you how the session went, which words got stronger and which were tough. A flashcard rating is your own judgement, so it no longer earns the bonus for a right answer or counts towards Know it all, and familiar words are recalled by typing more often.

features.title: Flashcards
features.text: Flip a card and the translation is right there, big and clear: no more hunting for it behind an icon. In the card settings you can pick a direction: recalling the word from its translation is harder but better for speaking, and “Both ways” switches sides from card to card. You'll also find shuffled order and read-aloud there: the word plays when you show the answer. Every card shows how firmly the word sits in your memory. Cards sit in a deck: take the top one off and the next word is already waiting underneath. The front is warm, the back is calm, and flipping no longer flashes bright in dark mode. A big set goes in rounds of 20 words, and Kolo remembers where you stopped, even halfway through a round. At the end of a round you see your tough words and can run through them again until none are left. The summary is honest now: it tells you how the round went, compares it with last time and shows your path through the set. Swiping right now means “Remember”, not “Know”, and while you drag the card it shows which rating you're about to give. And “Study” on a set's page opens the mode picker, just like in the list of sets.

features.title: Quiz
features.text: The quiz is now an exam on your set: 20 questions (or 10, or the whole set), starting with the words you got wrong last time and the ones that are due. Answer by choice, by typing or a mix — in a mix, weak words come as a choice more often and strong ones as typing, and now and then you answer by ear. A correct answer moves on by itself, three in a row start a streak, and the sound climbs with it. After the quiz you can go straight into a mistake review until every word is right. Kolo remembers how many words of the set you've got right, compares your score with last time, notes a set record and celebrates when the whole set is passed. A mistake on a word you haven't learned yet no longer upsets your schedule, and the bonus for a flawless quiz now starts at 10 questions. Each question sits on a card, like in flashcards, with the word's strength and part of speech, and the answer sheet in the header shows how your result is shaping up. Don't know? Tap «I don't know» instead of guessing.

features.title: Blitz
features.text: The speed round is now called Blitz, and its minute works for your memory: due and weak words come first, and a word you miss comes back a few questions later. A short 3-2-1 countdown starts the clock, and if you leave the app, the round pauses. After a mistake the right answer stays on screen a little longer while the clock keeps running, so guessing doesn't pay — and when you really don't know, there's “I don't know”. Every set keeps a record: the header shows when you beat it, and the summary compares your score with last time and lists the words you missed, with sound. You can be asked the other way round, both ways or by ear. New words are just for play here: they no longer land in your schedule, Perigee introduces them. A round counts from 10 answers, and the Speed demon achievement can now be earned in Blitz too.

features.title: A plan for every set
features.text: Tap Study on a set and you'll see its plan first: how many words are strong, growing, still learning and new, and when the whole set will be in rotation. You set the pace yourself — 5, 12 or 20 new words a day — right there or in Settings, and the estimate moves with it. Every set card in Words shows the same plan as a thin bar.

features.title: A course for every language
features.text: Norwegian over here, Spanish over there: each course has its own sets and folders, so nothing gets mixed up. Pick your language once and switch courses right from the header.

features.title: Weekly orbits
features.text: Instead of flames that go out after a single missed day, you get a weekly goal of 3 to 7 days. Hit it and your orbit closes and your streak grows. A shield covers a rough week, and a broken streak can be repaired in the first three days of the next one.

features.title: XP and levels
features.text: Every session and game earns XP, and your level grows with it. If you practised before, the XP for every card you've studied is already yours.

features.title: Capsules and collections
features.text: New levels and closed orbits bring capsules. Inside: satellites, ring colours, profile backgrounds and titles — 36 items across four collections. Duplicates turn into stardust, and stardust turns into a shield or a missing item. The odds are right there in the capsule window.

features.title: A brand-new profile
features.text: Your avatar in the ring of your choice, your level, your weekly orbit, a showcase of your three favourite rewards, medals and stats — all on one page. The higher your level, the more satellites fit on your orbit — up to three.

features.title: Thank you, beta testers
features.text: Everyone who joins before the end of 2026 gets a medal, the Beta Tester title and the First Orbit ring. After that, they're gone for good.

features.title: Settings that make sense
features.text: Account, appearance, learning, notifications and data — in short rows, like the settings on your phone, so you can see what's on at a glance. Email, password, sign-out, backup and account deletion live there too, in More → Settings. And the Other tab is now called More.

features.title: Sounds for practice and rewards
features.text: Answers, flashcards and games now have their own sounds: soft notes for right and wrong answers, a rustle when a card flips, a ticking clock in the last seconds of a Blitz round. New levels, closed orbits and capsules each get a fanfare of their own, and every rarity sounds different. You can turn sounds off in More → Settings.

features.title: Share a word
features.text: Any word in a set can become a picture for social media or a chat: tap the share button next to it. The card shows the word, its translation, explanation and example in a light, warm or night style. Send it straight from the share menu, download it, or copy it on a computer.

features.title: A livelier Kolo
features.text: The home screen now talks to you. Above the main button, a short line says what matters right now: how many days you've gone without practice, that one session today closes your weekly orbit, how many cards are left to your daily goal or how many you did yesterday — can you beat it? Every state has its own moving picture: words drift off orbit when it's time to review, new words fly in to join it, and the moon comes out when you've had enough new words for the day. On a wide screen the words circle your daily goal. Every fifth right answer in a row gets a cheer in the quiz, Blitz and Perigee sessions, and the daily reminder no longer says the same thing every day.

fixes: Flashcards remember every rating again: because of a bug, only the last card of a session was saved.
You can practise without internet: sets you've opened before load offline, and your ratings are sent once you're back online.
Rated a card by mistake? Undo it with the arrow button at the top or with Backspace, and the card comes back from the side it flew off to.
Leaving in the middle of a session? Kolo shows how much is left and asks if you're sure: only a finished session counts, and your answers are kept either way.
The card no longer jumps when you reveal the answer.

The quiz forgives small things: a typo, missing special letters or a forgotten article count as correct, and the exact spot is highlighted right in the word: extra, missing and swapped letters. If your answer is also right but the card doesn't list it, add it to the card — from then on the quiz will accept it. Your phone no longer autocorrects foreign words as you type.
The quiz opens again: a bug closed it right after the set loaded.
Practising a whole set before it's due no longer pushes words months ahead, and words due today are waiting from the morning on.
Progress is now counted by the server, so it can't get lost or faked.
A session done offline no longer disappears — it counts as soon as Kolo is back online.
The new Orbit design and a new heading font.
Writing to support is simpler: pick a topic, type your message, and we'll reply to your account email. Messages with characters like _ or * now send without an error.
New here? A short intro and First steps on the home screen take you from your first set to your first session — with hints along the way.
The home screen no longer says everything is reviewed while new words are waiting, and a set's page now has a Study button.

Folders work properly: rename and recolour them, delete only after a confirmation (the sets stay), the Back button closes a folder, and after a session you return to the same folder. You can create a folder straight from a set’s menu, and starred sets from folders show up in Favourites.
The daily reminder now speaks your app language and counts words waiting for review.

Kolo opens faster: your words and sets appear straight away and refresh quietly in the background, and switching tabs no longer flashes a blank screen. The home screen no longer says “Start with your first set” or “0 words” for a moment while loading.
Words you add to a set now show up straight away on the home screen, in Words and in First steps, without reloading the app. A set’s page opens instantly too.

Search has moved from the header to the Words tab: type a word or translation at the top and you'll see which set it's in. Tap a result and the set opens right on that card. Letters like é or ü can be typed without the marks. On a computer, ⌘K or Ctrl+K takes you there from any tab.

If two words share a translation, the second one no longer shows up among the answer options, where a right answer used to count as a mistake. Type a synonym in the quiz, and Kolo will recognise it and ask for the other word.

Flashcards and the Perigee session show the same answer sheet in the header as the quiz: a cell per word, coloured by your answer. And a long set name no longer pushes the header buttons off the screen.
“Play again” right after a round no longer shows answer options that don't match the word.
A Perigee session no longer shows a “—” answer button when two words share a translation.
Kolo now updates when you come back to it, not only after a restart, and never in the middle of a session. In More you can see which build you have and check for updates yourself.

The loading screen no longer looks frozen on a slow connection: the satellite circles the logo, and if loading takes longer than usual, Kolo tells you what's going on: still loading, a slow connection or no internet at all. In the dark theme it no longer flashes white.

versions.title: Kolo on your home screen
versions.intro: You can now install Kolo like an app, and there are three games for quick review.

features.title: Install Kolo
features.text: Add Kolo to your phone's home screen or your computer's dock: it opens full screen, without an address bar, and updates itself.

features.title: Three games
features.text: Speed Round — answer as many as you can, with a streak multiplier for right answers. Survival — three lives, each mistake costs one. Match — pair words with their translations before time runs out.

features.title: Profile photos from your device
features.text: No more hunting for a link: pick a photo from your phone or computer and Kolo compresses it for you.

features.title: Your own @username
features.text: Every account now has a unique username. You can change it in your profile.

features.title: Tighter on phones
features.text: Home, Profile and Other are much more compact: fewer giant cards, more of what matters on screen. The activity calendar fits your screen and achievements fold into a short list.

fixes: The back of a flashcard no longer overlaps the front.
The mobile browser toolbar no longer covers buttons at the bottom of the screen.
Pages you open often appear instantly, without extra animation.
The My words / Kolo Sets switch now spans the full width on phones.
Sets no longer disappear when you delete a folder.
The daily game no longer gets confused by time zones, and emails no longer show on the leaderboard.
Daily reminders move to the next day correctly.
